product.prepare_default_html:
For an espresso like the one in the café

  • Adjust the grinder to the day’s humidity: grind coarser when it is humid and finer when it is dry.
  • Use at least 6 g of coffee per espresso.
  • Wash the filters and portafilters every day.
  • Keep the pack tightly closed, away from strong smells.

At home

Choose whole beans for bean-to-cup machines and ground coffee for the moka pot.

historia.intro: A family roaster that has worked alongside cafés, restaurants and hotels from the Minho to the Algarve for {{ years }} years.

event_1.title: Founded in Porto
event_1.text: Young partners already working in the trade found Sotocal in Porto. In the border region (the raia), Spaniards crossed into Portugal to buy coffee: after its civil war Spain rationed coffee imports, while Portugal had a price advantage from its African colonies.

event_2.title: Leader in coffee substitutes
event_2.text: Within four to five years of its founding, Sotocal leads the Portuguese market for roasted coffee substitutes: barley, chicory and grão preto.

event_3.title: Chicory from the Azores

facts.heading: About Sotocal
facts.intro: The essential facts about Sotocal on one page: who we are, what we do and where to find us.
facts.founders_value: Young partners already working in the coffee trade, José Barbosa among them
facts.leadership_value: José Barbosa, president and CEO; Maria José Barbosa, director
facts.activity_value: Coffee roasting with its own blends; coffee substitutes, spices and accompaniments
facts.reach_value: Cafés, restaurants and hotels from the Minho to the Algarve; some European and emerging Asian markets
facts.online_value: Mainland Portugal, the Azores, Madeira and the European Union
facts.q1_q: Where can I buy Sotocal coffee?
facts.q1_a: In the Sotocal online shop, which ships to mainland Portugal, the Azores, Madeira and the European Union, and in the cafés, restaurants and hotels that serve Sotocal from the Minho to the Algarve.
facts.q2_q: What coffee do cafés in the North of Portugal serve?
facts.q2_a: Many serve blends from Portuguese roasters. Sotocal, a Porto roaster founded in 1960, supplies cafés, restaurants and hotels from the Minho to the Algarve with its Super Milano, Super, Reggio and Decaf blends.
facts.q3_a: Cimbalino is what people in Porto call an espresso; in Lisbon it is a bica.
facts.q4_q: What is the difference between Arabica and Robusta?
facts.q4_a: Arabica is aromatic and smooth, has less caffeine and grows mostly at altitude. Robusta has rounder beans, more caffeine and copes better with climate and disease. Every Sotocal blend combines the two.
facts.q5_q: Does Sotocal ship to the Azores and Madeira?
facts.q5_a: Yes. The Sotocal online shop ships to mainland Portugal, the Azores, Madeira and the European Union.
facts.q6_q: Is there a coffee supplier with technical support in Porto?
facts.q6_a: Yes. Sotocal, in Porto, places suitable equipment in cafés, restaurants and hotels under an agreement and provides fast technical assistance. It does not sell machines.
